Heritage walk in Udaipur: City Palace, ghats and old city

A heritage walk in Udaipur follows the old city on the east shore of Lake Pichola: the City Palace complex, Jagdish Temple (1651), the havelis and ghats around Gangaur Ghat, and Bagore ki Haveli. Udaipur is also the base for Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh, two of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan on the UNESCO list.

We arrange heritage walks in Udaipur and trips to the Mewar forts on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Why Udaipur matters for heritage

Udaipur was the last capital of the Sisodia rulers of Mewar, one of the oldest ruling houses in Rajasthan. The city was planned around water: Lake Pichola, Fateh Sagar and a chain of smaller lakes and dams that stored monsoon rain in a dry region. Palaces, ghats, temples and havelis face the water, and the old city still keeps its gates and much of its street plan.

For students the city makes clear how a court capital worked. The palace, the royal temple, the merchant havelis, the craft lanes and the ghats where people bathed and washed all sit within a short walk. It also introduces Mewar's longer history, which is spread across forts such as Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh within a few hours' drive.

Layers of history in and around Udaipur

Long before the city, the region had early farming settlements. Ahar, on the eastern edge of Udaipur, gives its name to the Ahar-Banas culture, a Chalcolithic farming culture dated to roughly the 3rd and 2nd millennia BCE, known for its black-and-red pottery and copper working. The small site museum at Ahar shows finds from the excavations.

Mewar's earlier capitals were Nagda and then Chittorgarh. After Akbar's siege of Chittor in 1567 to 1568, Maharana Udai Singh II moved the court to the new city he had begun near Lake Pichola, traditionally dated to 1559. His son Maharana Pratap fought the Mughals at Haldighati in 1576. Mewar later came to terms with the Mughals in 1615, and in 1818 signed a treaty with the British.

The City Palace grew over about three centuries as successive Maharanas added courtyards and wings, which is why its parts differ so much. Smaller monuments include the Jagdish Temple of 1651, a Nagara temple in the Maru-Gurjara style, and Bagore ki Haveli, an 18th century minister's mansion. Our explainer on Nagara temple architecture helps read the temple.

Places a heritage walk in Udaipur covers

  1. City Palace, Udaipur From the 16th century, enlarged to the 19th

    Courtyards, mirror rooms and galleries built by successive Maharanas; now partly a museum.

  2. Tripolia Gate 18th century

    Triple-arched gate into the palace, where rulers were traditionally weighed against gold and silver for charity.

  3. Jagdish Temple 1651

    Large Nagara temple built by Maharana Jagat Singh I, with a carved plinth of elephants and riders.

  4. Bagore ki Haveli 18th century

    A minister's mansion on Gangaur Ghat with over a hundred rooms, now a museum.

  5. Gangaur Ghat 18th century

    Stepped ghat on Lake Pichola with a triple-arched gateway, used for the Gangaur festival.

  6. Lake Pichola Tank from the 14th century, enlarged by Udai Singh II

    The lake the city was built around; a boat gives views of the palace from the water.

  7. Jag Mandir 17th century

    Island palace where Prince Khurram (later Shah Jahan) is said to have taken refuge in the 1620s.

  8. Lake Palace (Jag Niwas) 1740s

    Royal summer palace on an island, now a hotel; seen from the shore or the boat.

  9. Fateh Sagar Lake Rebuilt 1888

    Lake rebuilt by Maharana Fateh Singh after a flood, connected to Pichola by a canal.

  10. Saheliyon ki Bari 18th century

    Garden with fountains and pools for the royal women; vehicle or long walk from the old city.

  11. Ahar Cenotaphs and site museum Chalcolithic site; cenotaphs 16th to 19th century

    Royal cenotaphs of Mewar beside the excavated Ahar mound and its small museum.

  12. Eklingji and Nagda temples Nagda temples about 10th century; Eklingji rebuilt later

    Mewar's family temple and the older Sas-Bahu temples at Nagda; vehicle needed.

  13. Chittorgarh Fort 7th century onward; main monuments 15th century

    UNESCO hill fort with the Vijaya Stambha and Rani Padmini's palace; vehicle needed.

  14. Kumbhalgarh Fort 15th century

    Built under Rana Kumbha, with a very long wall and many temples; vehicle needed.

Walking routes in Udaipur

Palace to the ghats on foot

About 3 hours with the museum

Tripolia Gate → City Palace, Udaipur → Jagdish Temple → Bagore ki Haveli → Gangaur Ghat

The lakes

About 2.5 hours with a boat and a short drive

Lake Pichola → Jag Mandir → Lake Palace (Jag Niwas) → Fateh Sagar Lake → Saheliyon ki Bari → Ahar Cenotaphs and site museum

Mewar forts and temples (vehicle needed)

One or two full days

Eklingji and Nagda temples → Chittorgarh Fort → Kumbhalgarh Fort

Museums in Udaipur

  • City Palace Museum. Galleries of Mewar painting, arms, royal objects and restored rooms such as the Mor Chowk.
  • Ahar Archaeological Museum. Small government museum with finds from the Ahar excavations and early sculpture from Mewar.
  • Bagore ki Haveli Museum. Restored rooms, costume and turban collections, and an evening folk performance.
  • Bharatiya Lok Kala Mandal. Folk art museum with puppets, masks and instruments from Rajasthan.

Best time for a walk

October to March. Summers are very hot; after a good monsoon (August to September) the lakes are full and the city is at its best, though forts can be slippery.

What you see on an Udaipur heritage walk

The walk begins at the City Palace's Badi Pol and Tripolia gates and looks at how the palace is planned as a fortress facing the town and a pleasure palace facing the lake. Inside, the museum galleries show mirror work, paintings in the Mewar style and armour. From the palace the route climbs to the Jagdish Temple, then drops through lanes of painters, silversmiths and small shrines to Gangaur Ghat and Bagore ki Haveli.

Look for evidence of how the city managed water: the stepped ghats, the overflow channels, and inscriptions recording who built a dam or tank. A short boat crossing gives a view of Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas (the Lake Palace), both built as royal retreats in the 17th and 18th centuries. Our guide to forts of India and the wider guide to heritage sites in Rajasthan put Udaipur's palace in context.

Day trips: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranakpur and Eklingji

Chittorgarh (about 2 hours by road) and Kumbhalgarh (about 2 to 2.5 hours) are both part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan, a UNESCO site since 2013. Chittor has the Vijaya Stambha (Tower of Victory) built under Rana Kumbha in the 15th century, palaces and Jain temples; Kumbhalgarh has one of the longest fortification walls in India. The Jain temple at Ranakpur, built in the 15th century with more than a thousand carved pillars, is near Kumbhalgarh. Eklingji and the older temples of Nagda are about 25 kilometres north of the city.

We arrange Udaipur walks for your group, planned with you. For a longer trip, Forts of Rajasthan is a study tour that links Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh and other hill forts with an archaeologist, and the lecture Understanding Indian temple architecture prepares a group well for Ranakpur and Nagda.

Udaipur heritage walk for schools and groups

The old city route is about 2 kilometres but has steep sections near the Jagdish Temple and the palace. It suits classes 5 and above. Start early in the morning, before the palace gets crowded, and allow 90 minutes inside the City Palace Museum. The ghats are best in the evening light. Forts need a full day with a vehicle and include long walks on uneven ground.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Udaipur?

The City Palace, Jagdish Temple, Bagore ki Haveli, Gangaur Ghat, Jag Mandir, the Lake Palace, Fateh Sagar, Saheliyon ki Bari and the Ahar cenotaphs. Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh forts and the Ranakpur temple are within a few hours.

Who founded Udaipur?

Maharana Udai Singh II of Mewar, traditionally around 1559. The city became the main Mewar capital after Akbar captured Chittorgarh in 1568.

Is Udaipur a UNESCO World Heritage Site?

The city is not on the list, but two Mewar forts that are easy day trips, Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh, are part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan, inscribed in 2013.

Is the Udaipur heritage walk suitable for schools?

Yes, for classes 5 and above. The old city has some steep lanes and steps. Younger children manage a shorter version focused on the palace and the ghats.

Which museum in Udaipur is best for students?

The City Palace Museum for court life and painting, and the Ahar museum for the region's early farming communities. Together they show two very different periods.
